results.title: Athens Mayor Opposes Handing Bloodstained 1973 Uprising Flag to His Own Party
results.description: Athens Mayor Haris Doukas has come out against plans to hand the bloodstained flag of the 1973 Athens Polytechnic uprising to his own Socialist PASOK party. He said the symbol of resistance to Greece's military dictatorship "belongs to the Greek people." "The flag of the Polytechnic does not belong to any party. Not even to the party I belong to," Mr. Doukas said, after iefimerida reported that the flag would be given to PASOK. He proposed that it instead be entrusted to the Greek parliament, "as a symbol of our democracy," or to the Association of Imprisoned and Exiled Resistance Fighters, whose members were jailed, exiled and tortured under the junta. "It is a symbol of unity, a symbol of the popular uprising," he said. The flag flew over the Athens Polytechnic in November 1973, when students occupied the campus in protest against the 1967-74 military regime. The revolt was crushed on Nov. 17, when a tank smashed through the gates. Dozens of people were killed in the crackdown. leads an annual march to the U.S. Embassy each Nov. 17, and Greece marked the 53rd anniversary this week. Mr. Doukas has been seen as an internal rival to PASOK leader Nikos Androulakis. Διαβάστε περισσότερα στο iefimerida.gr
